title: Blob Storage Basics
description: Learn about Azure Blob Storage, its three blob types, and how to choose the right storage tier.

data.text: Azure Blob Storage is Microsoft's object storage solution for the cloud. Think of it as a giant, scalable hard drive in the cloud that stores unstructured data like documents, images, videos, and backups.

data.title: Blob Types
items: **Block blobs** — Best for most scenarios. Stores text, images, videos, and documents. Made of blocks that can be managed individually.
**Append blobs** — Optimized for append operations. Great for logging and streaming scenarios where you only add data to the end.
**Page blobs** — Stores random access files up to 8 TiB. Used for VHD files that back Azure Virtual Machine disks.

data.text: Azure Blob Storage offers three access tiers that let you balance cost against performance. Choosing the right tier can save you significant money.

data.title: Pro Tip
data.text: You can set a default tier at the container level, or override it for individual blobs. Lifecycle management policies can automatically move blobs between tiers based on age.

terms.definition: Binary Large Object — a file of any type stored in Azure Blob Storage
A unique namespace in Azure that gives you access to your blob, file, queue, and table storage
A grouping of blobs, similar to a folder in a file system

data.title: Create a Storage Account and Container with Azure CLI
data.content: Run these commands in Azure Cloud Shell or your local terminal with the Azure CLI installed.
data.code:
# Create a resource group
az group create --name myResourceGroup --location eastus

# Create a storage account with Hot tier
az storage account create \
  --name mystorageaccount123 \
  --resource-group myResourceGroup \
  --location eastus \
  --sku Standard_LRS \
  --kind StorageV2

# Create a blob container
az storage container create \
  --name mycontainer \
  --account-name mystorageaccount123

# Upload a file to the container
az storage blob upload \
  --container-name mycontainer \
  --name myfile.txt \
  --file ./myfile.txt \
  --account-name mystorageaccount123

# Set the access tier on a blob
az storage blob set-tier \
  --container-name mycontainer \
  --name myfile.txt \
  --tier Cool \
  --account-name mystorageaccount123

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Blob Storage stores unstructured data like files and media
Three blob types: block, append, and page blobs
Hot tier for frequent access, Cool for occasional, Archive for rare
Use Azure CLI to quickly create accounts and upload files
data.takeaway: Blob Storage is your go-to for files in the cloud. Start with the Hot tier and let lifecycle policies move old data to Cool or Archive.
